summary:
Ruby is ported to the shared README tutorial, root quick start and REFERENCE page at interface v3. I worked in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f1977c62-4748-5872-8f72-6f448dbac3f1/scratchpad/design/proto2/pilot-rb/sdkgen and started from v3-frozen (8d5ad97b). The one command passes: `REGEN=1 ./portcheck.sh <clone> <out> rb` gives `PORTCHECK rb: PASS`, with 0 unclassified and 0 defects in every section, purity at 0 open and 1 accepted, and the guard at 3/3. The Ruby README lane (`node --test --test-name-pattern '^rb: ' dist-test/generatedcompile.test.js`) went from 48/49 on OLD to 49/49 on NEW. The one OLD failure was 'the README examples run with Basic auth and a templated server' ('the README has no templated server'), and the shared S49 server option fixed it. before/run.sh ran every block on the default, crud and basic-server models: OLD and NEW each executed 4 root, 20 README and 21 REFERENCE blocks on default and 4/18/14 on crud and basic-server. Every run reported '4 runs, 20 assertions, 0 failures'. The repo suite without the toolchain lanes passed 2549 of 2554, with 5 skipped and 0 failures. The provider reads no model, and the hook calls only the generator's functions. I extracted rbSdkFile into utility_rb and Main_rb now calls it.

Continuing needed one shared change, which is additive and touches only test tooling. The guard's forms reader could not find a Ruby method declared with no parameter list (`def options_map`), so I added an optional `bare` field to forms.ts. I found four more interface gaps and did not implement them:
- `prints: 'fields'` cannot express Ruby's old choice of fields in the tutorial list and the whole record elsewhere.
- The chosen fields come from the example entity but are applied to a different, nested load entity.
- showFields compares types to '$STRING' while the model writes them with backticks, so it never picks a display field and prints only the id.
- The shared dataGet sentence drops "Returns a copy of the current data." That fact is true of the rb, py, php and perl runtimes.

Lines: the three old components were 745 lines (530 without blanks and comments). The provider plus hook is 178 lines (137), the guard forms 66 (57), and other rb files +11 (6). The worktree measurements (lines.js) still label rb 'not ported'. Ten catalogue issues were fixed with no Ruby-specific code. One old Ruby fact was dropped (data_get returns a copy), and Ruby's README Reference table (not ported) now disagrees with REFERENCE.

guide_problems.problem: Forms cannot declare a method that has no parameter list, which is Ruby's normal form. findDecls skips such a declaration, so the guard reports the member undefined. The default sigName/sigParams/sigReturns also need '(' (fixable per language), and ReadmeRef's memberName regex needs '(' too. Shared change required (made, additive)

The guide points at P/freeze/my/classify.js but does not say: (a) copy my/ beside your tools copy (it resolves ../tools and ../harness); (b) classify.js rewrites tools/classes/<lang>.json for EVERY language with templates under tools/review, so a baseline run of another language there gets rewritten; (c) after a passing portcheck the templates hold only unclassified classes, so re-running classify.js or allclasses.js sees nothing. Per-outcome counts need a rerun with CLASSES pointing at an empty directory

There are two corrections sources. tools/corrections.json (blocks.js 'after corrections') has no rb entries. The harness/corrections.js normalizers used by blockexplain.js limit several entries by language regex to the ported eight (for example server-required-given is c|zig|clojure|rust|elixir). A new port therefore gets 'after corrections 0' and must explain every changed block class by hand (26 whys for rb), and its counts are not comparable with the baseline table

'prints: fields' is presented as a simple choice. The guide does not say that it changes every shown entity (tutorial load and root quick start, where OLD rb printed the whole record), that the fields come from the example entity even when the load entity differs, or that showFields picks no display field under backticked model types

'A null-argument form chosen per operation ... cannot be kept (the provider sees no operation name)' is wrong as stated: the call statement carries s.op, and printers index facts.method with it. What is true is that a per-operation choice would need an operation literal outside the fact tables, which purity flags

'deleting your three components changes three lines, and nothing else' is wrong when section 1's own instruction (extract a naming function, make the generator call it) is followed. rb's golden changed 11 lines, all rb's own

Deleting the components with `git rm` stages them, so the first plain `git commit` of the shared file sweeps the deletions into the shared commit. The guide should say delete with rm and stage by path, or commit with explicit paths

With REGEN=1, gen.js SKIPS alias-go2 ('alias staging would write into the clone; copy the clone under tools'). The guide does not mention it, so the 21-variation claim silently becomes 20 (irrelevant to rb, relevant to go ports)

The guide says to read example.ts and sdkdesc.ts. To know what the page would print I also had to read ts/src/cmp/ReadmeQuick.ts (which statements use show(), step titles, notes), ts/src/cmp/ReadmeRef.ts (memberText sentences per kind, memberName needing '('), helpers/runtimeprose.ts (which facts the sentences take), test/runtimefacts.test.ts (findDecls and the no-parameter-list failure), and test/generatedcompile.test.ts README_LANES (what the ^rb: lane runs)

Any hook that adapts example names with exampleVarName gets the same finding ('naming function no non-README component calls'), which must be accepted with the py reason. The guide could say this finding is expected

gaps: Ruby did not run the blocks of all 21 harness variations. The README lane runs its own 13 models, and before/run.sh runs default, crud and basic-server. A variation-specific block (doc-nested root load, ref-issues collision) is checked by structure only

Not implemented: interface gaps 2-5 (prints granularity, per-entity show, showFields backtick comparison, dataGet copy sentence). They are recorded only, because shared changes from a port are discouraged
